contract.known_boundary: Normalize app visibility/foreground-background transitions, close/exit requests, and headless process shutdown through target-specific adapters.
contract.non_equivalence_policy: Flutter AppLifecycleState, native mobile process lifecycle, desktop window-close events, browser beforeunload, and Unix/headless shutdown signals are distinct event sources and are not treated as semantically interchangeable.

candidates.event_source: Android ProcessLifecycleOwner and iOS application foreground/background notifications
native desktop close interception and browser beforeunload

candidates.raspberry_pi_evidence: Pure Dart shutdown package uses ProcessSignal; Raspberry Pi OS/Linux supports POSIX process signals. Runtime hardware validation remains open.

candidates.event_source: detached child/parent process watchdog via Process.start
candidates.raspberry_pi_evidence: Pure Dart process-watchdog design is Linux-compatible research evidence only; package SDK constraint is Dart >=2.16 <3.0 and therefore it is not current-runtime ready.

research_findings.mobile: app_lifecycle_protector supplies the framework-level lifecycle boundary on all standard Flutter targets. flutter_fgbg independently sources Android process lifecycle and iOS application notifications, avoiding a false two-wrapper independence claim on mobile.
research_findings.desktop: app_lifecycle_protector covers framework suspend/resume semantics while window_manager and flutter_window_close expose native window close/lifecycle boundaries. Desktop shutdown and app visibility remain distinct concerns in the draft contract.
research_findings.web: app_lifecycle_protector covers Flutter lifecycle/visibility semantics while flutter_window_close implements a real beforeunload handler. Browser unload is not treated as equivalent to foreground/background state.
research_findings.raspberry_pi: Depth is 2/2 through two mechanically distinct headless shutdown families: isoos/shutdown uses ProcessSignal, while dart_graceful uses a detached parent/worker watchdog. Neither is hardware/runtime certified; dart_graceful is additionally constrained to Dart <3 and would require replacement or modernization before admission.
research_findings.security: flutter_fgbg and shutdown are fully CLEAR in live pinned preflights with OSV checked and no hits. app_lifecycle_protector is source/supply-chain CLEAR but remains REVIEW because logging ^1.2.0 was unresolved for SBOM/OSV. dart_graceful is REVIEW because Process.start is a HIGH source finding; no upstream code was executed. lifecycle, window_manager and flutter_window_close are pinned research candidates whose live scans were deferred solely by GitHub API rate limits and are not security admitted.

decision.next_action: Keep discovery depth closed but admission open: complete deferred pinned scans after GitHub rate-limit reset, resolve app_lifecycle_protector dependency versions, replace or modernize dart_graceful for Dart 3+, define normalized event ordering/debounce/termination guarantees, and run platform-specific lifecycle tests including Raspberry Pi process termination before Library intake.
